observed: Deeply divided star-like leaves with small marginal teeth; branching stalks bearing round heads outlined with long pointed projections. Native-resolution heads have green centres and blue rims.
support: The combination of palmately divided leaves and prickly-looking heads remains compatible with castor.
limits: A three-part capsule is not demonstrated. Colour boundaries are not capsule sutures. Individual pedicelled balls and long peripheral projections could represent other heads; peltate attachment is not securely proven. No reproductive sex or seed diagnostic established.
decision: Ricinus communis retained as provisional candidate, not confirmed.
review: Direct browser inspection of overview, enlarged region, and native-resolution crop. Dimensions and folio labels verified against Yale IIIF manifest. No image files downloaded.
alternatives: black gum / arctium / bidenus hypnis (Petersen compilation; spelling preserved)
independence: Researcher assessment after exposure to proposed identities; not blinded botanical identification. ELV provenance and alternatives retained from v77.

observed: Five-part flower outlines, blue and yellow paint; broad lanceolate lower leaves and deeply divided upper leaf-like structures. The native-resolution upper-right flower has one upper lobe, two lateral and two lower lobes, one lower lobe yellowish.
support: Different lower/upper foliage forms and five-part coloured flowers support a Viola/pansy comparison.
limits: Divided structures cannot securely be assigned as stipules rather than leaves. No diagnostic spur established. The drawing does not cleanly show the usual two-upper/one-lower pansy petal arrangement; orientation and stylization remain alternatives. Species and modern subspecies unresolved.
decision: Viola, with V. tricolor as a candidate, retained; no exact species anchor.
